title: SteadyThought: Mitigating LLM Under-Thinking via Thought-Level Preference Optimization
claim: Models switch among many thoughts before reaching a correct one; our framework finds switching points and optimizes preferences to commit to promising paths.
layout: 3 panels: two scatter plots stacked left, large three-tier pipeline right, top-to-bottom flow
description: The left column has two stacked scatter plots. Panel (a) is red dots for DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B on MATH-500, and panel (b) is blue dots for Qwen3-8B on AIME2024. Both plot the number of thoughts (x) against the rank of the first correct thought position as a percentage (y), and the dots follow a decaying curve. The right panel (c) is a framework diagram in three rounded boxes, read from top to bottom. The top blue box, 'Identification of Thought Switching Points', shows an entropy curve with a dashed threshold above a row of thoughts T1 to Tn drawn as gray circles, with explicit markers and red switching-point dots. The middle orange box, 'Trajectory Synthesis', has a robot icon and regenerated thoughts T1' to Tn-1', each marked with a red cross or a green check. The bottom green box, 'Fine-Grained Preference Optimization', pairs an input of question plus T2 with a chosen continuation T2' and a rejected sequence T3 to Tn. The eye goes first to the colorful pipeline on the right.
caption: (a) Rank of the first correct thought position for DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B on MATH-500. (b) Rank of the first correct thought position for Qwen3-8B on AIME2024. (c) Overview of the ST framework, which identifies thought switching points using two complementary signals: explicit linguistic markers and concurrent entropy spikes around step boundaries. Starting from these identified junctions, the model is guided via logit control to generate persistent reasoning continuations, effectively verifying the potential of the current thought. These synthesized paths are then used to construct fine-grained preference pairs for the STPO objective, which reinforces trajectory commitment at the exact point of divergence to effectively mitigate under-thinking and improve reasoning efficiency.
abstract: Flexible switching between reasoning trajectories (i.e., thought switching) has significantly enhanced the reasoning capabilities of Large Reasoning Models (LRMs). However, existing models often switch excessively yet fail to sustain promising reasoning thoughts, a phenomenon termed "under-thinking". While recent efforts suppress switching to mitigate this, such over-correction may discard valuable trajectories. To address this challenge, we propose Steady Thought (ST), a novel thought-level preference optimization framework. ST formalizes under-thinking as a preference issue at switching points, forcing single-path continuations from identified points to yield high-quality reasoning. Then, ST performs thought-level preference optimization by treating the newly generated response as preferred and the original one as dis-preferred. Experiments across multiple models and datasets show that ST effectively reduces token consumption, achieving reductions of up to 63.8%, while maintaining strong reasoning accuracy. Further analysis suggests that ST helps models acquire a generalizable ability to reduce redundant switching across domains and languages. Code is available at https://github.com/MIRALab-USTC/SteadyThought.
